basis: Developmental disability and limb defects define syndrome; intrinsic reflux 11/16 and hearing impairment 7/13. Myopia 5/11 omitted under four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: intrinsic oesophageal dysfunction with reflux in 11/16 (~69%) is a common syndrome manifestation.
decisions.ocular: none: myopia in 5/11 (~45%) qualifies, but less frequent ocular impairment is omitted under the four-axis cap.

basis: Skin/nail abnormalities, marrow failure and oral leukoplakia are defining dyskeratosis congenita features; marrow failure 1/3. Other organ complications lack qualifying frequencies.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: oral leukoplakia is part of the major diagnostic mucocutaneous triad of dyskeratosis congenita; oral mucosa maps to gastrointestinal.

basis: Immune-mediated medium-artery vasculitis; cutaneous PAN predominates among single-organ presentations, supporting skin damage in >30%. Other organ sites vary.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: cutaneous PAN is the predominant single-organ presentation, supporting >30% with direct inflammatory skin injury; skin is not universal across this umbrella.

basis: Myopathy, leukoencephalopathy and ocular dysfunction define disease; ptosis 6/6 and ophthalmoplegia 3/4. Dysphagia and respiratory failure reflect muscle dysfunction.

decisions.ocular: primary: ocular dysfunction is a named, defining component; ptosis occurs in 6/6 and external ophthalmoplegia in 3/4.

basis: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and developmental olfactory dysfunction define the Kallmann phenotype; hyposmia 2/4, anosmia 1/4. Osteoporosis 2/8 is below threshold.

decisions.neurologic: primary: olfactory developmental dysfunction is a defining Kallmann component, explicitly represented by anosmia in the name; hyposmia 2/4 and anosmia 1/4.

basis: CoQ10 biosynthesis disorder; neuropathy and neurodevelopmental impairment occur commonly (>30%). Supplied renal, cardiac, pulmonary and hearing findings lack established frequencies.

decisions.neurologic: involved: neuropathy/neurodevelopmental impairment is common (>30%) across COQ7 deficiency; the disease is defined by CoQ10 biosynthesis deficiency rather than a required neurologic lesion.

basis: Carcinoma originates in eyelid epithelium; eyelid is ocular, and the usual cutaneous epithelial origin also establishes the skin axis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the usual origin is eyelid skin epithelium, supported by the explicit skin carcinoma parent; ocular and cutaneous origins overlap here.

basis: Defined by congenital ocular abnormalities, neurodevelopmental impairment with progressive spasticity, and hypogonadism. Contractures follow neurologic spasticity.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: contractures follow progressive neurologic spasticity; the record does not establish direct disease of skeletal muscle, bones or joints.

basis: Partial tyrosinase deficiency is an inborn melanin-synthesis disorder, defining skin/hair hypopigmentation and ocular developmental abnormalities with impaired vision.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: OCA1B is an inborn metabolic defect of melanin synthesis from partial tyrosinase deficiency; the metabolic mechanism axis applies.

basis: Zellweger disease defines peroxisomal, cerebral and hepatic pathology; pachygyria 11/14, hepatopathy 2/4. Tricuspid regurgitation 2/4; ocular/renal/hearing frequencies not established >=30%.

decisions.hepatic: primary: hepatopathy is a defining component of the Zellweger phenotype; hepatomegaly and elevated transaminases each occur in 2/4.
decisions.neurologic: primary: cortical developmental abnormalities are a defining Zellweger feature; pachygyria occurs in 11/14, with hypotonia 3/4 and seizures 2/4.
